units.function: Small UI helper that distinguishes text/binary portability entries, infers image MIME from a short extension map, creates base64 data URLs and classifies image previews.
units.dependencyDirection: UI-only code depends on the shared file-entry type and browser data-URL semantics. It has no core/domain ownership.
units.keyDataModels: CompanyPortabilityFileEntry, extension-to-MIME map, nullable text/content-type/data-URL results.
units.lifecycle: Prefer declared contentType; otherwise infer from filename extension; interpolate declared base64 into a data URL; classify image/* for preview.
units.testAssessment: No direct focused tests were found. Invalid base64, conflicting extension/MIME, mixed-case/compound paths, SVG behavior, oversized content and malicious declared MIME are untested.
units.designRationale: Give the import/export UI a minimal way to preview text and common image files without a server round trip.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS Web needs safe previews for untrusted migration artifacts and evidence without letting package metadata decide executable/renderable content semantics.
units.companyOsFit: REIMPLEMENT in the independent Web adapter using server-verified MIME/digest/size metadata, an allowlisted safe raster preview path, bounded Blob/object-URL lifecycle and explicit download for unsupported content. Do not copy the data-URL interpolation helper.
units.responsibilityConflict: A preview can visually misrepresent evidence when declared MIME or extension disagrees with bytes; no verified digest/source context is shown alongside the rendered artifact.

securityFindings: The package-supplied contentType is trusted ahead of filename and actual bytes.
Any declared image/* becomes previewable, including SVG, without a safe raster-only allowlist or sanitization contract.
Large base64 strings are duplicated into data URLs, creating browser memory amplification and no revocation lifecycle.
Base64 validity, decoded size and digest are not checked in this UI boundary.
Preview classification is presentation-only and must not be treated as evidence-type verification.
